source_review.title: Direct evidence of the South Java Current system in Ombai Strait
source_review.citation: Sprintall, Wijffels, Molcard and Jaya (2010), Dynamics of Atmospheres and Oceans50,140-156, doi:10.1016/j.dynatmoce.2010.02.006
source_review.locator: Abstract, printed140 / PDF2; introductory southeast-monsoon calendar on printed141 / PDF3 read as text
source_review.prior_scope_distinction: The historical90nm cited cross-shore extent and this Ombai thermal-front confinement are different quantities. Neither becomes a paired velocity-boundary width.

records.name: South Java Current

reported_width_constraint.source_notation: within approximately10-15km of the northern boundary

records.geographic_scope: Northern Ombai Strait extension of the South Java Current. This is not a width assigned to the Sumatra-Java route.
records.layer: Surface-temperature/front interpretation associated with the SJC. The separately described50-100m velocity maximum is not a verified width-measurement layer.
records.time_convention: Southeast monsoon context, June-September in the introduction. The paper studies2004-2006 moorings, but no exact width occupation or monthly width sequence is supplied by this abstract statement.
records.boundary_rule: Authors suggest from surface-temperature maps that a front appears to trap the SJC near the northern boundary. No numerical velocity-edge threshold, paired edge coordinates or complete transverse velocity section is inferred here.
records.range_interpretation: Approximate one-sided confinement description, not a10-15km paired current-width range, annual min/max or confidence interval. No12.5km midpoint is assigned.
records.source_locator: Abstract, printed140 / PDF2; southeast-monsoon calendar from Introduction printed141 / PDF3
records.source_quality_note: The authors' tentative thermal-front interpretation is retained. It is not a new independent measurement or a uniform width of the whole current.
